comparator.name: Spatial Planning and Design
comparator.sourceNotes: Appendix 2.3–2.5 of the 2026–2027 regulations establishes the ordinary 180 EC pathway, including the Bachelor Project as one 15 EC component, 30 EC genuine choice and the compulsory methods progression. No named route applies.
components: 30 EC of approved electives, minor, exchange or supervised internship. No more than 10 EC of electives may be introductory first-year courses.
One 15 EC thesis spanning blocks 2a and 2b. Requires GIS, Statistics 2 and both qualitative and quantitative research methods.

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

core: Spatial planning, physical and institutional design, urbanism and the built environment
Climate, water, environmental systems, landscapes and physical geography
Planning governance, complex decision-making, economics, law and quality of life
Spatial evidence, GIS, statistics, qualitative and quantitative research
Creative design practice, design standards, studios, research philosophy and independent project work
adjacent: Climate-resilient cities, water systems and environmental planning
Urban systems, infrastructure, governance and institutional planning
questions: How can planning and design improve quality of life while managing competing spatial claims?
How can cities and rural areas adapt to climate, water and environmental pressures?
How can evidence, design thinking and public institutions guide spatial transformation?

alternatives.label: Spatial planning, environment & infrastructure
alternatives.concept: Use maps, environmental data and social research to study how places change. Combine spatial projects and water management with economics, sociology and public policy.
alternatives.labelReason: Geospatial projects, water management, social evidence and policy anchor a broad planning-related programme.
progression: Sustainability and research foundations precede Earth Observation, Spatial Planning and Living with Water. Economics starts in the first term. Current offerings and formal prerequisites pass.

alternatives.label: Climate-resilient cities & environmental systems
alternatives.concept: Study how places can adapt to flooding, climate change and pressures on water and land. Use geospatial evidence, earth science and ecology to evaluate responses.
alternatives.labelReason: Geospatial methods, delta adaptation, earth science, coastal ecology and energy design support environmental planning questions.
progression: The sustainability gateway precedes Earth Observation, Spatial Planning and advanced resource and energy work. Economics starts in the first term and Dynamic Earth is offered in the third. Current offerings and formal prerequisites pass.
alternatives.distinctness: 10 courses and 75 EC differ from the broad option in each direction. Climate risks, land and water systems, ecology and energy design are the focus.

alternatives.label: Urban governance & institutional planning
alternatives.concept: Study how public institutions and communities make decisions about land, resources and environmental risk. Combine applied spatial projects with governance, law, economics and public communication.
alternatives.labelReason: An applied Spatial Planning course anchors institutional and community questions developed through law, sociology and policy.
alternatives.distinctness: This option differs from the broad option by 9 courses and from the environmental option by 17 courses in each direction. Law, policy and participation provide the main emphasis.
progression: Both sustainability gateways precede Spatial Planning. The law gateway precedes constitutional, private and international law, and research methods precede advanced leadership. Current offerings and formal prerequisites pass.

selection.assessment: Three options give distinct weight to broad spatial evidence, climate and environmental adaptation, and public institutions. All use applied spatial planning. Each pair differs by at least 9 courses in each direction.

notes.text: UCR offers GIS and applied spatial projects, with options in water, climate and governance. Groningen also requires two design ateliers, mobility and infrastructure planning, and a 15-EC planning thesis.
Groningen’s third year reserves 30 EC for approved electives, a minor, an exchange or a supervised internship.

audience.programmeDescription: Spatial Planning and Design at the University of Groningen studies how places are planned and designed. Students use maps, research and design studios to investigate questions about mobility, water, land use and the environment.
audience.comparisonExplanation: All three UCR options include applied spatial planning. Their other courses emphasise broad spatial inquiry, climate and environmental adaptation, or governance and participation.
